scope: Newest complete eligible machine cycle not previously processed by Beta. T0 backpressure active; no ordinary expansion. Independent structural challenge limited to TER and SERV, the exact live exception items.
summary: No 1800Z machine delta changes the structural conclusions. TER's AI/advanced-package test bottleneck remains intact with concentration/cycle exposure as the principal counterweight. SERV's last-mile autonomy substitution case remains structurally plausible but capture depends jointly on utilization, permissions, partner access and financing. The open defects remain narrow underwriting reproducibility gates rather than structural-causal blockers.

claims: AI/HBM/advanced-package complexity continues to support higher production-test and known-good-device value, preserving Teradyne's bottleneck relevance.
Robotics remains a secondary labor-productivity pathway but is not a fully independent hedge because electronics/semiconductor exposure creates common-factor sensitivity.
No new machine evidence in 1800Z falsifies the established causal mapping; current SBC/debt/repurchase normalization is an underwriting gate, not a structural defect.
causalEdges: AI/HBM complexity -> advanced packaging/test intensity -> Teradyne test demand
advanced-package yield cost -> known-good-device screening value -> Teradyne/TEL test-cell relevance
manufacturing labor pressure -> cobot/AMR adoption -> Robotics demand
falsifiers: Critical AI-device test shifts materially to substitute/captive architectures that reduce Teradyne content per device.
AI/semiconductor capex contracts while Robotics remains too correlated to diversify the shock.
risks: Customer concentration and semiconductor capital-cycle sensitivity remain structural counterweights.
unknowns: Durability of test intensity per AI device across architecture transitions.

claims: Short-distance delivery labor/cost continues to create a real substitution pathway for autonomous sidewalk delivery where density and permissions support utilization.
Partner/category breadth may improve utilization but announcements alone do not establish economic capture.
No 1800Z delta falsifies the use case; financing/runway and concentration remain upstream underwriting gates that can prevent capture without negating the structural opportunity.
causalEdges: last-mile labor/cost -> sidewalk autonomy substitution -> Serve demand
partner/category breadth -> route density/utilization -> fleet economics
falsifiers: Utilization cannot absorb fleet, remote-operations and maintenance costs.
Platform access or municipal permissions narrow materially.
Human intervention intensity remains incompatible with attractive unit economics.
risks: Capital intensity and financing can interrupt the causal path before scale economics emerge.
unknowns: Paid-delivery density and contribution margin in mature markets.
Remote-assistance economics at current fleet scale.
